utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, The Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, to my colleagues on the Defence and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis for the Prosecution, assisted by Alma Imamovic-Ivanov our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much and for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to my colleagues from the OTP, to everybody in and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Delic with legal assistant Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon to you, sir, Mr. Dedovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony yesterday to tell the truth the whole truth and nothing else but the truth, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dedovic.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yesterday, sir, I asked you a number of questions about meetings and I wanted to just touch on a few other topics concerning any meetings that General Delic may have had during the time-period that you were serving as his body-guard. We spoke yesterday, sir, about, in particular corps commanders, meetings with corps commanders and my first question is are you aware of any other meetings that General Delic may have had with Main Staff officers, such as Mr. Jasarevic or Mr. Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attend such meetings. The commander did have these meetings, but I did not attend them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And so I take it then, sir, that you're not familiar or aware about what was discussed at any of those meetings between General Delic and Mr. Jasarevic or Mr. Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because I was not present at the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, as part of your duties or responsibilities, did you personally have any contact with any officers of the ARBiH military security in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because I belonged to General Delic's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Same question, sir, with respect to any communication that you may have had with military -- ARBiH military security in the forward command post in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about with any ARBiH military security personnel who may have been stationed at the -- in the Gloc at Visoko?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not have or maintain any contacts with members of military security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, let me ask just a few questions concerning any planning or preparatory steps that you needed to take as part of your duties concerning the protection of General Delic. When you were planning trips or making visits outside of Sarajevo, did you have any meetings with any military security or military intelligence people, in terms of determining threat assessments against General Delic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any contacts with representatives of military security or military intelligence. I was serving in the corps without any contacts with the military security administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not sure if this perhaps was a translation error. You say you were serving in the corps without any contacts? Is that what you said, sir, or is this perhaps a translation error?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no I wasn't serving in the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Oh okay. Let me ask you this: Did you, prior to -- well, let me just ask you in more general. During the time that you served as the body-guard or escort to General Delic, were you making any assessments to any security threats against his person?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How did you do that, sir? What did you do? Who did you consult with? What type of information were you consulting?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When going -- I would go out into the field and by seeing what the situation was out in the field, I would change the routes we took, but I did not consult anyone, including military security administration on these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I take it, then, from your previous answer what you were doing in effect was some kind of advance trips, going into the field and making these independent assessments on your own. Is that what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't make assessments in advance of the trip, but I would make my decisions as we would go out into the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you would be -- would you be travelling, sir, in the same vehicle as General Delic during these trips in the field?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the same vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, can you explain to us, sir, how, if you were in the same vehicle with General Delic you would be in a position to be making determinations as to which routes should be taken, if you were in the vehicle at the time? What type of information were you relying on to make these assessments?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my own assessment, and I never used the same route twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What did you base these assessments on?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was for security reasons as a preventative measure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. But let me just make sure that I understand what you told us a few moments ago. At any point in time during the war when you were serving as General Delic's protection officer, did you receive any specific information about threats to him, to his person from any outside source?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never received any sort of information that would deal with the -- that would be a security threat to General Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me turn then to another topic that you testified about at length yesterday and that concerns communications. I believe yesterday and I don't have, unfortunately, the full paginated version. But yesterday at page 7 of the transcript, sir, you told us in response to a question from Madam Vidovic that among your duties or responsibilities was to announce that General Delic would be visiting specific places or locations. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I take it, because of the nature of your work and the position that General Delic held, that these announcements were not something, as a general rule, that would be made available to the public?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, they would be made available to the public; or no, they would not be made available to the public?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would not be available to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I believe, sir, you also told us yesterday, again, this is reflected on page 39 and 40 of the transcript, that during the Sarajevo operation that commenced in early June 1995 and which ran until the end of August 1995, General Delic was constantly at forward command posts and touring various units in different corps to establish coordination among those units with respect to the Sarajevo operation. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness never made such a statement. Did he not give this time-frame. Quite the contrary, he described a series of trips he made with General Delic in the month of July. That is why the Prosecutor should specify the time-frame the question refers to. Otherwise, the question as put is confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, the Prosecutor has specified a time, early June 1995 to August 1995, and if he is misstated, I'm sure the witness can correct him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me just ask a couple of other questions just so that we're all clear we're talking about the same thing. Can you tell us, Mr. Dedovic, in the period from June through August 1995 what was happening with respect to operations concerning Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The period between June and end of August; is that the one you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And in 1995.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the month of June, the Sarajevo operation commenced. The commander was engaged throughout the time on the Sarajevo theatre of war. In the month of July, to be precise on the 11th of July, Srebrenica fell or rather the Srebrenica enclave did. As far as his engagement went, of course he was busy on that score. Next -- or, rather, we were in the area of Tuzla and Kladanj until the 19th when we went to Split where a conference was held known as the Split declaration. At the end of August, we went on the trip to Iran -- or, rather, at the end of July we made that trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say, We were in the area of Tuzla and Kladanj until the 19th; do you recall which month and year you were talking about when you made the reference to Tuzla and Kladanj and the 19th?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The month of July. From the 17th to the 19th of July, 1995, that's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during this period, again from June through August 1995, based on what you've told us, would it be fair to say General Delic had a rather extensive travel schedule?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was rather busy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, sir, because of the nature of General Delic's position, I take it that his travel during that time-period would have been something that you would have wanted to keep secret?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't just me who wanted to keep it secret. It was probably also the Presidency deciding about the travel and the trips.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, regardless, sir, of who -- upon whose initiative it was, it was certainly the case that General Delic's travel schedule and travel plans was not something that you would want to be revealed to the public for fear that the enemy would know where he was and when. Would you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. His personal security and safety would be threatened in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, Mr. Dedovic, you told us about the telephone systems and how those were unreliable as a form of communication during the war. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The communication system was very poor and highly unreliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us then, sir, how it is that you coordinated or made the announcements necessary for General Delic's travel schedule in the period from June through August 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since in that time-period we were out in the field, there was no need for me to make any announcements. It was on the commander's discretion that we went to the various areas where combat activities were taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, sir, during this time-period what you're telling us then is that General Delic would just decide tomorrow we go to Tuzla or Kladanj and you just go there, without any of these announcements being made in advance?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The General did not make such decisions in advance. If we happened to at Proskok he and -- he would say, Let's go into the direction of the AOR of the 2nd Corps. We didn't have reliable communication system that would allow us to make such announcements at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And just so we're clear then, sir, is it your testimony that in the period from June through August 1995, during this period of extensive travel by General Delic, that none of those plans were announced by you? You simply went from one place to another during that time-period, wherever General Delic decided to go?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would be travelling with the General wherever he wanted to go without making any announcements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I take it though that the trip to Split during this time-period would have been something that wasn't just decided at the last minute by General Delic. There would have been some kind of planning and announcements and communications concerning that trip, would there not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about the plans for that trip. I know that we had five minutes to get ready for that trip, and we were -- we had a change of clothes in the vehicle as we were travelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, whether there were any plans in place or security teams, additional security teams that would be present at these locations where General Delic visited to protect him and to supplement the protection that you and Admir Delic could give the General?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the forward command posts, there was security in place that secured the said locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you weren't able to communicate with those forward command posts and tell them that you and General Delic were coming. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because I did not have the authority to issue orders to these members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir -- well, let me ask you a different question. Yesterday, and this is reflected on page 8202 of the transcript at lines 17 through 19, in reference to the operations again in the summer of 1995 concerning Sarajevo, you said the commander was directly involved in combat actions. The commander was directly involved in combat actions. Do you remember saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander was present in some of -- in some parts of the battlefield while combat activities were ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, that's my next question. What do you mean when you say he was directly involved in combat actions? What do you mean by that, "directly involved"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander directly commanded and controlled the Sarajevo operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were there any other operations that the commander directly commanded and controlled during the war; or was there the only operation, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, that was the only operation that the commander commanded and controlled personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, sir, if during this period when this operation was going on General Delic was travelling in Tuzla and Kladanj and Split and Iran, how is it possible that he directly commanded and controlled the Sarajevo operation?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his absence, within the control and command system, he had his deputies, Chiefs of Staff, who assumed that responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you're telling us, sir, in that time-period there was not an ability or not a means by which General Delic could communicate with these deputies and Chiefs of Staff?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were able to meet up directly out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you give us an example, sir, of one of these meetings out in the field? A time and a place perhaps?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember these meetings out in the field, because the commander was constantly touring the field.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, have you been asked by the interpreter to repeat the last sentence of your answer, if you could, please. They didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander was not holding meetings because he was busy touring the territory where combat activities were taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused because a moment ago, as reflected on lines 8 through 11 of this page, you told us in response to my question they were able to meet up directly out in the field. And now you've just told us the commander was not holding meetings because he was busy touring the territory where combat activities were taking place. And so my question to you, sir, is if General Delic was busy travelling or touring the locations of the combat activities, how was he able to have communication with the people who were commanding and controlling the Sarajevo operation?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly in the field by touring all the sections where combat actions were being carried out, he had to see for himself what the situation was in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, Mr. Dedovic, can you please give us some examples of locations that you're referring to that were in the field. Again, during the Sarajevo operation, during that period in the summer of 1995.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Proskok, Visocica, Orahovo, Nisici plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, if during the time period around the 19th of July, 1995, when you have told us that the commander was in the areas of Tuzla and Kladanj, was he still able to command and control the Sarajevo operation during that time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was away from the Sarajevo front, somebody would take over those duties. One of his subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, was General Delic able to communicate with these subordinates during this big operation while he was away from the Sarajevo front?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because he did not set up this communication through me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. I take it then from that answer it's possible he was in communications with his subordinates at the Sarajevo front but simply you weren't aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because when we were out in the field, we didn't have a reliable means of communication. We didn't have portable phones for him to maintain the system of communications. As to if -- to whether he did maintain communication with them or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, during these times let's just go back to these locations that you mentioned: Proskok, Visocica, Orahovo and the Nisici plateau. At the time in the summer of 1995 that you and General Delic were touring these locations were those places close to the front lines and was there active fighting going on at the time you were in those locations in the summer of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was active fighting going on. These were active sections of the front where combat actions were continuously going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you visited these four locations in the summer of 1995 while this active fighting was going on, did you provide any advance communication or advance notice to any of the ARBiH units at these locations that you and General Delic would be coming?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never informed any members of the armija that the General would be coming to any of those locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly then, Mr. Dedovic, you and General Delic drove into an area where there was active fighting going on without any advance notice to your own forces that you would be coming. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm not a security professional, sir, but it would seem to me that you would be putting your life and General Delic's life in danger by simply driving into an area where there were active combat actions going on, if only out of concern for being attacked by your own forces. Wasn't that a concern of yours?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not worried, because we were coming from our territory. As for that security aspect, we could have been killed in front of the Presidency building too, as far as that security aspect is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you didn't have any special concerns about being accidently targeted as friendly fire by ARBiH forces during this time-period in the summer of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we could not have become a target at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me turn to a different subject. Yesterday, sir, you told us that General Delic was only rarely, I believe was the word used, rarely in Kakanj during the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the war General Delic maintained a home or a residence in Visoko, did he not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did, but he was rarely there, because most of the time we spent actually touring the territory. We were not in one place for long.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And Visoko is approximately how far from Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20 to 25 kilometres, I think. Taking the motor way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at any point during the war was the motor way between Visoko and Kakanj in enemy hands.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was possible that it could be hit by artillery fire from the Kiseljak direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: True. But that wasn't the question. My question, sir, was whether at any point during the war that motorway was actually in enemy hands?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that as of 1993 it was not in the hands until the end of the war, but before 1992, I am not familiar with the situation in that section of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. But certainly during the time-period in the war when General Delic was the Main Staff commander the road linking the forward command post or the command post in Kakanj and General Delic's residence in Visoko, that road was held by BH army forces?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dedovic, during these time-periods when you and General Delic were travelling abroad -- I'm going to ask you some questions about these places that you went to when you were travelling outside of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Let's start with the times you were in Croatia whether it was Split or Zagreb or anywhere else. During those periods when you were in Zagreb or in Split or in Croatia where did you stay? Did you stay in hotels or private residences or where did you stay?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At hotels. In Split, we were at the Villa Dalmatija. That is where we were staying. It's a hotel compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall where we were staying in Zagreb when you travelled to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a hotel. I don't know exactly which hotel it was. I don't know the name, but it was a hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you and General Delic were staying at these hotels in Split or Zagreb, did you stay in the same room or did you have separate hotel rooms?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Separate hotel rooms, but my room was always in the immediate vicinity of the General's room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about the trip that you made to the Islamic Republic of Iran in the summer of 1995. Where did you stay when you were in Iran?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In hotels also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during that stay, sir, did you also say in separate hotel rooms that were in the close proximity to each other?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very close, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple of questions about this trip to Iran. Do you recall, sir, or did you have any discussions with General Delic about why you were going to Iran?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't talk to General Delic about why we were going to Iran.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And coming -- I assume you flew to Iran. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we took the plane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you remember, sir, on that trip to Iran where you flew from, where you departed from, going to Iran?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Pula airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you flew back to Pula as well?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that we also landed at Pula airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on the aeroplane, I'm just curious, did you sit next to the General during those flights to and from Iran?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity of the General. In front of him or behind him, but in the immediate vicinity, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And coming back from Iran, did you have any discussions or did he say anything to you about what was discussed during his meetings in Iran?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The General did not comment with me about what was going on in or what -- what had been going on in or what happened in Iran.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And so just we're clear then during the time you were going to Iran and on the way coming back from Iran you didn't have any discussions with General Delic as to why you were going or what had happened or whether it had been successful or what was discussed in any of the meetings?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never had such conversation with the General, me asking what had happened at a meeting or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I wasn't just referring to you asking. I was also referring to perhaps General Delic perhaps would have made a comment to you. The meetings were successful, or we talked about this. Or anything along those lines. Without you asking, I'm just wondering if he volunteered any information, any small talk or any conversation about what was discussed or why you were going.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I found out what it was all about only when this was published by the newspapers when it was broadcast on television about what happened during General Delic's trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What did you hear, sir, about this trip from the media, the newspapers or the television?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it was a visit that had to do with aid to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of aid?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but some kind of assistance was planned. I don't know what kind of assistance though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me just ask you then, sir, a few questions about the trip to Malaysia that you made with General Delic in the late summer/early autumn of 1995. When you flew to Kuala Lumpur, where did you fly from? What airport did you fly from?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we left from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you returned also to Zagreb, to the Zagreb airport, from Kuala Lumpur?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we landed at Zagreb airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during the time-period, sir, that you were in Kuala Lumpur, I think yesterday us you were staying at a hotel. And my question to is the same as earlier. Were you and General Delic in the same hotel room or were you in separate hotel rooms that were in the close or immediate vicinity to one another?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in separate rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, either on the way to Kuala Lumpur or on the way back did you have any, again, discussions or conversations with General Delic about the purpose of that trip or the results of any meetings that he attended while he was in Kuala Lumpur?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't speak to him about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were in Kuala Lumpur, I know you -- you spoke yesterday about telephone conversations. Do you know if General Delic had any telephone conversations in his hotel room while you were in Kuala Lumpur?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, he did not have any telephone conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you don't know if he called his wife or his family or anyone like that, any of his personal acquaintances while he was in Kuala Lumpur?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because those contacts would have been made through me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we just hold it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you know you have already answered but we had some problems with the transcript so I'm going to ask the question again and ask you to answer it again, so it is on the record. My question was while you were in Kuala Lumpur were you aware of any phone conversations General Delic may have had with his wife or his family or any of his personal acquaintances?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, General Delic did not conduct that kind of conversation, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to a different topic, sir. I'm going to be discussing with you different dates and places where General Delic was during the period from roughly the end of July until the end of September 1995. Sir, do you recall being in Kakanj with General Delic on the 29th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown PT2352. And if we could start actually by going to page 12 in the Bosnian. We can stay on the first page in English. We can go to page 12, the last page in the Bosnian. Sorry, it should be page 14. I think there's a pagination error in the original. The last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the signature at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's General Delic's signature, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Would you need to consult an expert, handwriting expert. I'm not really qualified to say if that is General Delic's signature or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever see General Delic's signature during the course of the war?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I am saying this signature doesn't mean anything to me. I'm not qualified to decide whether this is General Delic's signature or not. I cannot assert that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I understand that. That wasn't my question --

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your testimony, sir -- you were the body-guard or an escort for General Delic for, I believe, you said seven years, from June of 1993 until he retired from the army in 2000. So for seven years you were this man's escort and body-guard and you never once saw his signature, you're not familiar with his signature?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever get performance evaluations or anything like that from General Delic during the time that you were in the army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't get any assessments relating to my work performance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's go back then to the first page of this document in the Bosnian. Sir, do you see on the upper left part of this document where it describes what this document is about? Do you see that on the document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Possibly this is some kind of a consultation. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, the subject line of this document says: "Conclusions and tasks stemming from the meeting held between the core members of the General Staff of the RBiH army and the corps commanders in Kakanj on 29 July 1995." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I put to you, Mr. Dedovic, that this document is signed by General Delic and refers to a meeting, it is a lengthy document; it is more than ten pages long. It refers to a meeting that General Delic held in Kakanj on the 29th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your assertion. You can assert whatever you like. I'm not going to go into your assertions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In late July 1995 and specifically on the 29th of July, 1995, sir, were you with General Delic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably. It is probably some kind of consultative meeting or something and that it lasted for a couple of hours. I was probably there. Definitely I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during such a consultative meeting that lasted for, as you put it a couple of hours, it very well may have lasted long than that, because it is a very lengthy document what would you have been doing? Would you have been in the room or outside the room?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have been saying so far, I never attended any meetings, consultations or anything, any kind of meetings. I would always be in front of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And is it your testimony, sir, that you were in Kakanj with General Delic on the 29th of July, 1995 or not, or do you simply not remember?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall it by that date, but I must have been there. I mean, if it was held, then we must have been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we ask that this document be marked for identification and I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document PT2325 is marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit number 1365, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1365, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. Perhaps we can check this. I am almost sure that this document has already been admitted. Maybe it was tendered through the -- from the bar table, but this is maybe something we should check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar assures us that it has not been admitted, and we will take her word for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dedovic, on either the 1st or 2nd of August, 1995, were you with General Delic in Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long were you in Zavidovici on that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how long, but we were there for a couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where did you go in Zavidovici on that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically what you mean, where did we go in Zavidovici. The question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me put it a different way. Sir, did you visit the headquarters or the command of the 35th Division of the 3rd Corps in Zavidovici on the 1st or 2nd of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which unit it was, but we were visiting one unit. I don't know exactly which unit it was though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, were there -- other than General Delic, were there any other senior officials who were present in Zavidovici on that day at this unit that you visited?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. President Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown P02358. And if we could please go to page 2 in the Bosnian and page 4 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, in the middle of page do you see paragraph number 3. It talks about combat morale?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Section 3. The second paragraph under section 3 refers to President Izetbegovic, General Delic, 3rd Corps Commander Mahmuljin, visiting the command of the 35th army division. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 35th Division ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go back to the first page of this document in both the Bosnian and English languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the date of this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, does this document seem to refer to the meeting that I just asked you about, in Zavidovici on or about 1 or 2 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The General's visit to the 35th Division with President Izetbegovic and General Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would ask that P02538 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document will become Exhibit number 1366.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Dedovic, to the best of your recollection, sir, when you and General Delic returned from Kuala Lumpur and flew into the international airport in Zagreb, what was the date of that return to Zagreb? When did you arrive in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was on the 17th of September. Yes, 17 September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are you certain of that date, sir, that it was the 17th or is it possible that it was on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it could not have been on the 16th, because the conference in Kuala Lumpur finished on the 16th. And even if we had departed immediately after the close of the conference, still, it would have taken 13 hours and we would have arrived on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness be shown PT 6288?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dedovic, this is a BBC, British Broadcasting Corporation, news article and if you see, sir, in approximately the middle of the page in Bosnian, this news report indicates that the BBC's Zagreb correspondent Nada al Isa asked General Delic for his assessment of the situation and that that correspondent asked that question on the 16th of September?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any meeting involving Nada al Isa. I'm not familiar with that individual or with that conversation taking place on -- that's the 16th, the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's what the report seems to indicate, sir, that on the 16th of September, 1995 the BBC's Zagreb correspondent asked General Delic for his assessment of the situation, and it makes reference to General Delic having attended the OIC ministerial meeting in Kuala Lumpur and goes on to say: "But the interview given to our correspondent was conducted in Zagreb." And I repeat my question whether it is not possible that you were mistaken and that you were already in Zagreb on the 16th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. Sorry, sir. Just hold on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The Prosecutor interpreted or, rather, misinterpreted the document. The document does not state anywhere. It is stated that the correspondent from Zagreb spoke to him, but it does not state that the interview was made in Zagreb. Quite the contrary, if you look at the source it's radio Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's quite a different matter. And you will recall the witness's evidence yesterday that a radio correspondent was with them down there, so I don't want the witness to be referred to a misstatement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the English document is very clear it is the second paragraph, I'm happy to read it, it indicates the interview given to our correspondent was conducted in Zagreb. That's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can see that, and do you have anything to say about what Madam Vidovic is saying regarding that headline F source radio Bosnia-Herzegovina, Sarajevo, in Serbo-Croat, 1.00 GMT, 16 September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The only comment I could make is obviously the BBC monitors a number of foreign broadcast services, and it seems from the face of the document that the BBC is reporting from the information that it got there radio Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time and date indicated on the BBC report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, can I just understand it is what you're objecting to. This paragraph that Mr. Mundis is referring the witness to starts off by saying: "Our Zagreb correspondent, Nada al Isa today, (16 September) asked army General Rasim Delic, commander of the Bosnian army, for his assessment of the success of Bosnian army and Croat Defence council units over the past few days. General Delic attended the OIC, organisation of the Islamic conference ministerial meeting in Kuala Lumpur, but the interview given to our correspondent was conducted in Zagreb." Is there no such thing in the Bosnian version, because we can't read the Bosnian. We can only go with what we see in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, I didn't notice that part of the text, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't observe that bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, would it be possible that you may have left on the 16th and you would arrived on the 16th also, since there was a difference in time, you said seven hours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We definitely were not in Zagreb on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember at what time you left from Kuala Lumpur? On the 16th, you said, on the 16th. At what time did you leave? Was in the afternoon, was it the evening, was it the end of the morning; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was late in the evening that we left, and we could not have arrived in Zagreb on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one little thing. Are you aware that when you travel from the east to the west there is this thing that they call -- you gain time? You may be in the air for 13 hours, but when you get to your destination, depending on how far it is from where you moved from, it may not be -- it may still be the day before the day you left. The concept of gaining time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is what the phenomenon is, in fact, but we were not in Zagreb on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders this is document as it goes to the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1367.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the document is already been assigned a number, and I did not have the opportunity to react. Therefore, I want to state the following: I oppose the admission of this document along the same principle whereby a document which the Defence used to challenge the credibility of Witness Zilkic and there were definitely many more elements in favour of admitting that document, the document had not been admitted. I don't see that we are now in the same situation when it comes to the documents proposed by either the Defence or the Prosecution, the purpose of which is to challenge the credibility of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, Madam Vidovic, I am speaking for myself in the unfortunate position of just having no recollection of the documents submitted through Zilkic. I would prefer you, rather than refer me to another document to put the basis of your objection for admission of this document, just put your arguments and if -- if they are the same as the Zilkic arguments, just repeat those arguments.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness stated that the document was not accurate. But he is not familiar with the journalist, al Isa. He stated that he didn't know whether General Delic in fact had this interview, and the witness in fact did not either identify the document or confirm it. Likewise, I don't see how the witness's credibility can be challenged on the basis of such a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my recollection is that the document that my learned colleague tried to show to and have admitted through the Witness Zilkic was being tendered both for purposes of impeaching the witness but also for the truth of the matter contained in the document. All I can indicate at this point in time is clearly we have one document that purports to be reflecting an interview that was given certainly on the face of the document on the 16th of September, 1995 at some point prior to 1300 GMT. The witness had said they were not present at that point in time. We simply indicate that this is something that goes to the credibility of the witness on that limited point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Mundis, you're going back to the Zilkic. Anyway, you told us what was said in the Zilkic matter. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me state for the record, that when it came to witness Zilkic I was referring to MFI 814. But let me respond to my colleague Mr. Mundis when it comes to his arguments in relation to this document. First of all, this text is unsigned, unauthorised, and was carried --or by a news agency. First we have the radio Bosnia-Herzegovina mentioned and then this correspondent al Isa from Zagreb. The text was not authorised and its contents were fully refuted by the witness, which I believe are reasons enough for never allowing this document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, these matters all go to weight and not admissibility in our respectful submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In my respectful submission, this is way beyond the time for taking the break. We'll come back and deal with this matter when we come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber apologises for coming in late. We had to be considering the issue at hand just before we left. We've sort of looked at the transcript relating to the Zilkic document, and on a cursory reading of the two points it doesn't look like -- it is not apparent to the Chamber what the difference is. For that reason, this document will only be marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit 1367 will be exhibit marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd ask the witness be shown P06287, P06287.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Dedovic, this document is from the French news agency AFP dated 16 September 1995, and I draw your attention to the third paragraph where again there is reference to General Delic going on national radio. And I'm wondering, sir, if you're in a position to comment as to this news article concerning a national radio broadcast on the 16th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on this because I never heard this statement by General Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And would General Delic have been in a position to make a national radio broadcast on the 16th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He could not have appeared on national radio on the 16th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, I take it, sir, that that's because it's your testimony that he was still in Kuala Lumpur on the 16th of September.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask this document also be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is marked for identification, may it please be given an exhibit number. Exhibit -- the document will become Exhibit 1368, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Dedovic, turning to the period after you and General Delic returned from Malaysia, can you tell us, please, whether during the month of September 1995, after the trip from Malaysia, you and General Delic were in the area around Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late September, we were in the broader Vozuca area in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps, but not in Vozuca itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's why I ask, sir, in the area around Vozuca. Do you recall the date that you were in Vozuca, in the area around Vozuca or greater Vozuca in September 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in late September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown P06286, P06286.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Dedovic, this document, if you can look at the very bottom of the document in Bosnian, seems to be a publication of the 35th Division of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Do you see that, sir, at the very bottom of this article?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does say the 35th Division of the land forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would draw your attention if we could please go in the Bosnian to the bottom right-hand corner where it says: "Epilogue," and that would be perfect. And now if we could go to bottom of page 3 in the English version and continuing to the top of page 4 in the English version, so if can he can start with the top. Sir, I'd ask you to take a look at the part of the article, this paragraph entitled epilogue. I'd ask you to read that to yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we turn the page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, reference to the visit of President Alija Izetbegovic to Vozuca in September 1995, in this article?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the article it says that two days later the President of the Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic would also arrive in Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, were you aware of the fact that President Izetbegovic had gone to Vozuca in September 1995? Did you personally know that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I personally didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But towards the end of this article it indicate ago few days later the commander of the glorious army would come as well. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that part of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The reference to the commander of the glorious army, does that refer to General Delic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see here that this is an assumption that the commander of the glorious army would come.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us, sir, that you recall going to September -- going to Vozuca with General Delic or the greater Vozuca area at the end of September. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vozuca is a very large sector. We were never in Vozuca itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what specific area or areas within this Vozuca sector you and General Delic visited?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps. These are parts of Ozren towards Petrovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to the admission of this document. I believe that the Prosecutor has not established a sufficient basis for the admission of this document. The witness did not identify the document in any other way -- in any way. He said that he doesn't know that President Izetbegovic was there. He said that it was an assumption that the commander of the army would arrive, and he did not confirm anything from the document, and there is no link between the witness and the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe the witness testified that he and General Delic went to the greater Vozuca area in September 1995 and certainly a number of the issues raised by my learned colleague from the Defence would go to the issue of any weight that the Trial Chamber may decide to give to this document and not necessarily go to the issue of admissibility of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document will be marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will be become Exhibit number 1369, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dedovic, this visit to the greater Vozuca area in September 1995 that you made, do you know if that was in the area around Maglaj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are parts of the Ozren mountain. These are actually on the other side completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say these are parts of the Ozren mountain. What do you mean by "these are parts of the Ozren mountain"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area where we were staying, that region of Petrovo Selo belongs to the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps. The Maglaj theatre of war belongs to the 3rd Corps area of responsibility. We did not spend time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me turn to a different subject with you, Mr. Dedovic. Are you familiar with or have you ever heard of a publication called Prva Linija?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prva Linija are you thinking of the weekly or the daily paper?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Exactly. That's exactly what I'm thinking of, sir. Are you familiar with that publication?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an army newspaper Prva Linija, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what do you mean, sir, by an army newspaper? Can you tell us what you mean by an army newspaper?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a newspaper that mostly covered the events in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And who -- do you know who was the publisher or who was responsible for the publication of this journal?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, really. I don't know who the publisher was and who was responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, at any point in time when you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. I just want to get clarity. Sir, when you say that it's a newspaper that mostly covered the events in the army, which army do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what I can recall, actually, my best recollection comes in the post-war period. It's a paper of or was a paper of the army of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which Federation, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And the army of the Federation, is it something distinct from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I emphasised that my recollection of that newspaper is from the post-war period. During the war, I didn't have the opportunity to read the paper. I wasn't receiving it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that, sir, but would you please answer my question. My question is, is the army of the Federation of Bosnia a distinct institution from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your question is not clear to me. Please, could you explain it a little more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said this document from your recollection is a document of the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Federation. I'm asking you: Is the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina a different institution or is it the same institution as the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina that was led by General Delic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina is separate. After the peace agreement, a Joint Command was established and that was the joint army of the Bosnia and Herzegovina, so it would be the -- the joint army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Dedovic, let me just turn to the final one or two subjects that I'd like to discuss with you today. During the course of the war --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to my colleague Mr. Mundis. I just want to see that it is in the transcript here the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and then we also have suddenly the army of the Republika Srpska which actually the witness did not mention. So perhaps my colleague can clarify that the witness did not mention the army of Republika Srpska. I'm talking about page 37, lines -- lines 17 and 18. We have the words the army of Republika Srpska. Actually this is creating some confusion. The witness did not mention that, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, can you please try an answer my question once again. My question had been, is the army of the Federation of Bosnia the same entity or institution as the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina that was led by the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it is not the same entity. It is not the same institution. These are two different institutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Does that clear it, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me just ask a couple of follow on questions on this topic. Sir, do you know when the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina was established?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, in 1994 the Joint Command or the Joint Staff was created of the HVO forces and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And then in the subsequent period, this is the body from which the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina evolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when did the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina come into existence?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximate time-period. A year, for example?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was after the signing of the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what -- once the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina was established, did the ARBiH continue to exist, or did it cease to exist?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, would it be fair then to say that in effect the army of the Federation subsumed or took over what had been the ARBiH?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically what you mean, that it took over. Could you please clarify your question. I'm not quite sure I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the time the ARBiH -- or at the time the Federation, the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina was established, the ARBiH, in effect, ceased to exist. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you, sir, at the time that happened, you were a member of the ARBiH. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatically I was no longer a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina but a member of the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, in effect, sir, you didn't have to take any steps personally to go from being a member of the ARBiH to being a member of the army of the Federation of BiH. It was automatic, as you said.

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me now turn to the last one or two subjects that I would like to talk to you or talk with you about this afternoon, Mr. Dedovic. During the course of the war, 1993 through 1995, did you, sir, ever hear of a unit known as the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't. I haven't heard of the existence of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And are you saying then, sir, that even to this day you have never heard of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard mostly about the existence of the El Mujahed when I -- following these trials. During the war, I never heard of that detachment. The army number 25.000 men, 100 brigades, 500 battalions; so I don't know, I mean, I didn't even know it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. But certainly just so we're clear during the course of the war you never heard of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. During the war, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, during the course of the war did you know or did you ever observe any people who appeared to you to be foreigners serving in or with the soldiers of the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know on the basis of what I should have been able to recognise them as foreigners, whether they would not be speaking our language or what. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let me ask you it a slightly different way. Do you know or did you ever observe or were you aware of the fact that persons coming from African or Arabic countries were serving in or with units of the ARBiH?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see afro-asian members of the BiH army. Myself being a member of the BiH army did not have occasion to see any such members.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I wanted to be sure, sir, so that we're on the same page, if you will. I'm talking about the period during the war, 1993 to 1995. Is it your testimony that you never on any occasion saw any persons from African or Arabic countries serving in or with units of the ARBiH?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have the opportunity to see these men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, in December 1995 or into the first few days of January 1996, did you accompany General Delic to any trips to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: End of 1995, early January 1996? It is possible that we went there. That was already after the signing of the Dayton Peace Accords. The war had ended. It is quite possible that we went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In that time-period, again December 1995 first few days of January 1996, were you personally present at any point in time when General Delic met with or spoke to persons from African and Arabic countries?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, General Delic never met with them in that time-period. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much Mr. Dedovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Madam Vidovic, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, very few brief questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Dedovic, before I proceed. I have only a few brief questions for you. The Prosecutor asked you a series of questions which had to do with the announcement of your visits to other army units in various war zones. You also told us yesterday that you had radio sets of stations as a means of communication. Can you describe for us the following: What would have happened, if anything, had you announced such visits in the war zones?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since such stations constituted unreliable means of communication I did not make contact over them with other units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question had to do with something else. When you say unreliable means of communication, what does that precisely mean?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that at any given point of time, members of the army of Republika Srpska, being in possession of more sophisticated technology were in a position to listen in to such communications. They had far more powerful technology.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what bearing would that have, if any, on the security of General Delic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been a threat to his security. That's why it was not used in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You say it would not be used. Why? Is that related to any inherent dangers?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It would have been a security threat.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today you were shown some articles and reports. Let me ask you this: Unless I'm mistaken, yesterday, while indicating the members of the delegation who accompanied you to Kuala Lumpur, you mentioned the journalist Senad Kamenica. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall which media he worked for?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio and Television Bosnia-Herzegovina, the state television, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did that also subsume the radio?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know he was an employee of the Bosnia-Herzegovina radio television, and I don't know what that implied.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall any of his activities during the conference? Did he make any contacts with anyone?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't tell you that. I believe he is the person who is best placed to tell you if and who he made contact with.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Madam Vidovic. Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dedovic. You told us during your testimony yesterday that when General Delic was appointed to the post as Supreme Commander, he met considerable resistance and outright disloyalty in the beginning, and he had to suffer humiliation and a lot of difficulty in order to cope with that. My question to you is: In your opinion, was the General able to overcome that over time so that by the end of the war he had been able to establish respect about himself, so that he enjoyed the support and loyalty and respect of his subordinates in the army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was able to overcome that, but only with the support of the Presidency and the president of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Tell us a bit about that. When and how did the President of the Presidency intervene in support of General Delic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the very fact that he initiated actions against the disloyal commanders of the 9th and 10th Mountain Brigades, since the commander was unable to do that himself, of his own initiative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So are you saying that after the Caco and Celo incidents, General Delic was then generally enjoying support of all parts of his army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that after these incidents, the commander's enjoyed full support of all members of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I would have thought the same, but ... Another question relates to something that you mentioned to us in your earlier testimony, and that was the meetings that General Delic had, I think it was in Kuala Lumpur or it -- I could have been mistake it could also have been in Iran, but you said something that struck my mind. You said that a lot of people came to see the General because they wanted to know how they could help, what kind of assistance they could offer and so the General could tell them that we need this and we need that. Is that what -- is that a fair account of what you said?

utterances.speaker: ISMET DEDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was at the Islamic conference in Kuala Lumpur. All the participants in the conference wanted to have a word with Commander Delic about the type of assistance needed. I don't know anything specific about what assistance was offered, but I know that all the participants in the conference wanted to have a word with General Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
